title: My research on Adversarial Policies in MARL
text:
My name is Jonathan Vincent and I am a PhD student at the UKRI AI Centre for Doctoral Training in Practice-Oriented Artificial Intelligence. My research focuses on robustnes in Multi-Agent Reinforcemnt Lesrning (MARL). In this website I layout my current research, projects and publications.

This website is authored in Quarto.

title: Limitations of Opponent Masking
text: Building off the summer project in this project we present evidence that opponent masking underperforms in environments, like Go, which are heavily dependent on reacting to the opponent. We show this limitation by first deploying opponent masking in an ideal scenario in Go. We then repeat the experiment using a novel rules-based defence. Opponent masking was unable to defend the target model, however, due to the ease of the test scenario, the rules-based defence achieved a 100% win-rate. We believe opponent masking failed because it removes too much information from the model’s input space. Naively reducing the degree of masking improves performance, suggesting approaches that minimise the number of inputs masked could be effective

title: Research
text:
Practice-oriented AI is about bridging the gap between between complex problem domains such as those found in science and research, and AI algorithms and techniques that could be used to solve problems in those domains.
My research focuses on addressing adversarial polcies, a threat to the robustnes of Multi-Agent Reinforecement Learning (MARL).

My current research within the CDT
Currently I am looking at different methods for mitigating an adversarial policy once it has been detected. Previous works have used opponent masking to mitigate adversarial policy, however I have intital results showing that opponent masking underpefroms in certain domains. Based on these results I am now investigating ways of improving opponent masking.


Research by others I’m building on
My current research buids off “A Classification Based Approach to Identifying and Mitigating Adversarial Behaviours in Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents”. My main contributions being an exploration of the current mitigation strategy, and alternative mtitgation startegies which imrpove on it in certain domains.

title: GoAD
text:
At the end of the Foundation Year I looked at defending adversarial policies in Go. In the project I use a adversarial classifier to detect when an adversarial policy is being used, then switch to GNuGo a rules-based Go model.
The main contribution of this is the use of a rules-based model as mitigaiton strategy for adversarial policies.
